stories.body: Donald Trump said the United States and Israel would hold off on new strikes against Iran if a deal to end the months-long conflict can be reached rapidly. He said the proposed terms included reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending Iran's nuclear threat, while warning that US forces were ready for a far larger attack. The announcement followed reports of possible strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, a call in which Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly urged de-escalation, Iranian threats of retaliation against regional states that assist Washington, and reported drone and maritime incidents in Kuwait and off Oman. Iran had not publicly responded to Trump's statement.
stories.headline: Trump pauses planned strikes on Iran while calling for a rapid deal

stories.body: A homemade explosive device detonated outside the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant near Moscow's Kudrinskaya Square, killing at least three people and injuring 21, Russian authorities said. The National Anti-Terrorist Committee said an unidentified woman carrying the device was stopped by a security guard while trying to enter the restaurant, which was holding a private event; the woman, the guard and a visitor were killed. Authorities have not named the victims, identified a target or assigned responsibility, while reports differed over whether the device was remotely detonated and whether the woman knew she was carrying a bomb.
stories.headline: Bomb attack at a Moscow restaurant kills at least three and injures 21

stories.body: All 13 people aboard a Cessna Grand Caravan sightseeing flight were killed when it crashed near Peru's Nazca Lines after departing from Pisco, authorities said. The dead included 11 tourists and two pilots; officials identified the passengers as seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards. The aircraft lost contact with air traffic control shortly after takeoff and crashed in the Pueblo Viejo area, where fire engulfed the wreckage. The cause is under investigation, and the accident adds to a series of fatal crashes involving tourist overflights of the UNESCO-listed desert geoglyphs.
stories.headline: Tourist plane crashes over Peru's Nazca Lines, killing 13

stories.body: Russia said its forces struck fuel-storage facilities in the Ukrainian port of Odesa and a tugboat used by Ukraine's military in Mykolaiv, as attacks on Black Sea shipping routes have intensified and unsettled global grain markets. Separately, Ukrainian authorities said at least nine people were killed and 22 injured when Russia launched ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight. The attacks come amid a broader escalation in long-range strikes and reciprocal operations by Russia and Ukraine.
stories.headline: Ukraine and Russia intensify attacks on Black Sea ports and Kyiv

stories.body: Three people were killed and seven injured, some critically, in a shooting at an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday afternoon, city officials said. Police found the suspected gunman dead near the restaurant, though officials initially said it was unclear whether he was included in the reported death toll. Investigators believe there was one attacker and are still determining the shooter's identity and motive. A witness said he saw a person carrying an AR-style rifle emerge from the drive-through before another man fired at the shooter.
stories.headline: Three killed and seven injured in shooting at an Idaho fast-food restaurant

stories.body: Michigan reported cyberattacks affecting nine water systems, joining Minnesota, where more than 30 systems were targeted earlier in the week. State officials said the Michigan systems continued to operate safely, local operators addressed the issues and there were no known public-health effects. The FBI is investigating and has not identified a culprit, although federal agencies recently warned that Iranian hackers have targeted water and wastewater systems and other critical-infrastructure controls. The incidents involved technology used to remotely monitor and control equipment and did not necessarily disrupt water service.
stories.headline: FBI investigates as Michigan joins Minnesota in reporting cyberattacks on water systems

stories.body: A fast-moving, wind-driven wildfire swept through northwest Spokane, Washington, crossed the Spokane River and forced thousands of people to evacuate. The Old Trails Fire had burned nearly 4 square miles by Saturday evening, destroyed an undetermined number of structures and remained at zero containment. The fire unfolded as a heat dome brought dangerous, near-record temperatures across much of the western United States, with Las Vegas reaching 115F and forecasts of 116F in Phoenix and 118F in El Centro, California, heightening wildfire risk in already dry areas.
stories.headline: Wildfires force evacuations in eastern Washington as extreme heat raises risks across the West

stories.body: Advocates warn that roughly 20,000 unaccompanied migrant children could lose federally funded legal services as a government contract with nearly 100 providers expires. The organizations provide rights presentations in shelters and represent children in immigration proceedings, but say they do not know whether they will be allowed to continue seeing clients or who will take over the work. Providers say children who lack lawyers will be substantially more likely to be deported to countries they fled, while the Trump administration and the Department of Health and Human Services did not respond to requests for an explanation of the contract's expiration.
stories.headline: Thousands of migrant children in the US face greater deportation risk as legal-aid agreement expires

stories.body: At least 67 people have died in the mass migration crisis at Spain's North African territory of Ceuta, with bodies recovered near the Tarajal breakwater after tens of thousands of Moroccans crossed or tried to cross into the city. Reports said many died by drowning or were crushed against rocks as large crowds attempted the passage, and officials were arranging forensic and identification capacity for the dead. Border access from Morocco has since slowed and many migrants have returned, but Ceuta's president said several thousand people still needed to be sent back and that the city was not yet back to normal.
stories.headline: Ceuta migrant crisis leaves at least 67 dead as Spain moves to restore control

stories.body: Spanish authorities began installing a 500-metre floating barrier beside the Tarajal border breakwater between Ceuta and Morocco after the mass arrival of migrants earlier in the week. The barrier extends the existing physical boundary, with a line of buoys and patrol vessels providing protection, and is intended to prevent swimmers reaching Spanish territory. The government says the installation also addresses a recent Supreme Court ruling that barred immediate returns for people who reached Ceuta or Melilla by swimming because there had been no physical containment barrier at sea.
stories.headline: Spain deploys a floating barrier at Ceuta's sea border following mass crossings

stories.body: The European Union will hold an urgent meeting of interior ministers on Tuesday after the mass crossings into Ceuta exposed sharp divisions over migration policy. Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez accused some European partners of selfishness and disinformation, saying that almost all of those who crossed had returned to Morocco and that the influx had not created unauthorised onward movement into continental Europe. Italy, Denmark and others criticised Spain, with Italian officials linking the crisis to Madrid's migration regularisation policy, while far-right parties in several countries called for Spain to be excluded from the Schengen area.
stories.headline: Ceuta crisis intensifies political pressure on Spain and exposes divisions within the EU

stories.body: A wildfire triggered after a truck caught fire on the A-66 motorway near Casas de Millán in Cáceres forced the evacuation of about 800 residents from Casas de Millán and Grimaldo. The fire had burned 761 hectares and covered a perimeter of about 18.5 kilometres, though emergency officials said it lost strength overnight after firefighting operations. Authorities maintained the regional wildfire emergency plan at operational level 1 while assessing conditions; a separate fire in Badajoz left a firefighter with second-degree burns after his vehicle was overtaken by flames.
stories.headline: Wildfire in Cáceres forces the evacuation of 800 residents

stories.body: Scientists, engineers and environmental groups are pressing Spain's government and opposition to agree on a national wildfire strategy, arguing that political disputes over its name should not delay action. WWF says the country needs a durable state-level plan that shifts more investment toward forest management and prevention, identifies high-risk areas, manages at least 1% of national forest land annually and supports agroforestry and rural economies. A World Weather Attribution analysis found that human-caused climate change made the extreme fire-weather conditions in central Spain at least 20 times more likely than in a preindustrial climate.
stories.headline: Spain faces renewed pressure to establish a cross-party wildfire response pact

stories.body: Rodalies rail services on parts of the R4 and R8 lines are suspended from 2 to 9 August for the commissioning of a new Adif electronic signalling system at Castellbisbal. The R4 is affected between Martorell Central and Molins de Rei, while the R8 is affected between Martorell Central and Rubí Can Vallhonrat. Renfe has arranged replacement buses, including R4 direct services every 15 minutes and stopping services every 30 minutes; R8 buses will run hourly. Rodalies tickets will be accepted on replacement buses if validated at the origin station.
stories.headline: Rodalies R4 and R8 services are disrupted for construction works through 9 August

stories.body: Barcelona metro passengers are again reporting oppressive heat on station platforms as the city experiences its fourth heat wave of the summer. TMB says conventional lines cannot easily cool platforms because passing trains push hot tunnel air into stations, unlike the automated L9 and L10 lines. A pilot cooling system installed last year at Plaça Catalunya on L1 and Plaça de Sants on L5 remains in place, but no new anti-heat trial has been launched this summer. Passengers, particularly older people, described overcrowded platforms and poor air circulation.
stories.headline: Barcelona metro passengers endure the summer's fourth heat wave

stories.body: Catalonia has recorded 29 deaths and 55 injuries in beaches, swimming pools and inland waters since the bathing season began on 15 June, a 32% increase in fatalities from 22 at the same point last year. Fifteen people died at beaches, nine in pools and five in inland waters, while pools accounted for the highest number of injuries and are a particular concern for children. Civil Protection urged bathers to use designated areas, follow lifeguards' instructions and closely supervise children and older people, especially during the current heat and high attendance at bathing sites.
stories.headline: Catalonia records a 32% rise in bathing-related deaths during the first half of the summer season
